chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abdullah ibn Talha al-Nahdi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Four (people), a supplication would not be rejected for them until the Doors of the sky are Opened and it comes to the Throne – the parent for his child, and the oppressed against the one who oppressed him, and the one gone to perform Umrah until he returns, and the Fasting one until he breaks (the Fast)'.
ai.seo_question: Who are the four people whose prayers are never rejected in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights four distinct states of spiritual potency where supplication is uniquely receptive, emphasizing the metaphysical elevation of the parent's blessing, the justice of the oppressed, the sanctity of the pilgrim, and the devotion of the fasting believer. In Shia scholarship, these categories are often linked to specific Quranic verses that validate the immediate response to their calls, reflecting the interplay between human action and divine mercy. The inclusion of the fasting person 'until they break their fast' underscores the critical moment of Iftar as a peak time for answered prayers.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ali Bin Al Numan, from Abdullah Bin Talha Al Nahdy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Four (people), a supplication would not be rejected for them until the Doors of the sky are Opened and it comes to the Throne – the parent for his child, and the oppressed against the one who oppressed him, and the one gone to perform Umrah until he returns, and the Fasting one until he breaks (the Fast)’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Nu’Man from ‘Abd Allah ibn Talhah al-Nahdi from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘The prayers of four people are not turned back before the door to heaven opens and they move to the Throne: the prayer of a father for his son, the prayer of an oppressed against his oppressor, the prayer of one who perfonns ‘Umrah until his returning home and the prayer of a person fasting before breaking his fast.’”
